notes.title: Player feedback update 1.1.2 now live!
notes.notes:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25084809/03338a3bda43a98a44e503e17b5293f7d5ef587e.jpg[/img]

Hello starfighters!

After watching Xenoraid out in the wild for some months, we've collected some of the most common items of player feedback and addressed them. We also included some items we just quite didn't get done by release.

Overall the update evens out some of the rougher edges of the game, making it overall somewhat easier and player friendly.

The update is now live, and here's the list of changes:

- Restart option added to Pause menu and Mission Failure screen
- primary weapons' passive cooldown is now faster
- Advanced Weapon Coolant tech upgrade now reduces weapon heat generation in addition to shortening weapon lockdown duration
- last block of fighter repair price is now lowered according to actual repair need
- dense asteroid fields now last for a shorter time
- Chapter 4 boss now has less saucer enemy minions
- enemy energy shields now stay down longer and regenerate slower
- enemy energy mortar strike vessel now stays stationary for a maximum of 10 seconds even without receiving damage
- enemy energy shield vessels now recover from EMP stun with shields down instead of shields up
- heavy drones spawned from drone carriers can't fire immediately after spawning any longer
- Heat Transfer Chamber upgrade for the Flechette Cannon now increases damage at all heat levels instead of high heat level only
- ammo pickups in Survival now show an "Ammo Full" text when ammo is full
- Survival prelaunch menu screen Back button now navigates to Survival level selection, not main menu
- various graphical improvements
* the same fire and smoke effect is used for all gunships' destroyed weapon pods
* larger 75/100mm Cannon muzzle flash effect
* new end of mission splash text effect
* minor performance optimizations

We're also celebrating the update with a Weeklong Deal discount of 50%! Now's a great time to check the game out again, write a Steam review (we'd especially enjoy these), and recommend the game to a friend!

notes.title: Our favourite reviews so far
notes.notes:
Xenoraid has been out for a bit over a week now. Let's look at some of the awesome things that have been said about the game.

[h1]Steam reviews[/h1]

[quote=Jimmy Dali]Well i'm really hooked on this game ....big time! Mainly because of it's innovative stance. Instead of button mashing your way thru missions like so many other bullet hell games, you have to strategically time your shots so as to avoid overheating your guns. I'm glad the devs took this fresh & unique approach[/quote]

Thanks Jimmy! A main driver of Xenoraid's design was disappointment in how trivial and secondary the actual shooting is in most shoot'em ups. We just really enjoy shooting in itself, and we wanted to make a game that was very much about [i]shooting[/i]. And not at all about memorizing, which is pretty much as far away from shooting as we can think of.

[quote=the10kan]I very much like the way enemy ships react to player actions rather than just moving in scripted formations. Most alien ships have guns with a fixed arc of fire, and they actively maneuver to line up shots on you or to avoid colliding with asteroids. [/quote]

Yes, exactly this! We found out quickly that the awesome shooting mechanics we had in the game work the best in conjuction with as dynamic combat as we can get. Which is great, because that was our assumption and plan all along! We also wanted to inject as much "space dogfighting" feeling into the game as the broad vertically scrolling shoot'em up genre limits permit, and were happy with the way how it came out.

Xenoraid - no to memorizing challenges, yes to piloting and shooting challenges.

[quote=Likconater(of the Gamerholics Anonymous fame)]Fantastic! Looking for a bullet hell game? Xenoraid has got you covered, truth is we didnt go into this game expecting alot but once we started playing it we just couldnt stop[/quote]

We're always happy to please :) We always felt like marketing and positioning Xenoraid is not easy, but at least we seem to be winning over people once they give the game a go.

[quote=stubar]I'd recommend Xenoraid to anyone looking for a thinking man/womans shoot 'em up![/quote]

Amen, brother. Amen.

Well, to be fair, at about 10 minute point in Survival I'm not sure I'm able to think much, it seems to be all about the lizard brain right about at that time :)

[h1]Critic reviews[/h1]

The game hasn't been widely picked up by gaming sites for critic reviews, but we're expecting more to come. The haul thus far has been great!

[url=http://www.brashgames.co.uk/2016/10/06/xenoraid-review/]Brash Games[/url]
 gave the game a perfect 10 out of 10 review score:

[quote=Brash Games]From the second I started playing this game it had my full attention, it was an incredible experience and I got lost in hours of gameplay.[/quote]

This almost made us cry a little.

[url=http://www.gamingcypher.com/xenoraid-review-pc/]Gaming Cypher[/url]
 awarded the game 8.5 out of 10: 

[quote=Gaming Cypher]If you are a casual gamer who needs to kill some time, or even a competitive gamer for the leaderboards, you may want to add this game to your stockpile.[/quote]

Yes, we feel the game should definitely go into a whole lot of stockpiles. Hundreds, thousands of stockpiles!

[url=http://operationrainfall.com/2016/10/04/review-xenoraid/]Operation Rainfall[/url]
 gave the game a solid 4 out of 5 stars: 

[quote=Operation Rainfall]Shmup experts may find the game less difficult than some bullet hell games for example, but the game still requires accuracy and good timing.[/quote]

Yes! We always knew the game wouldn't appeal to bullet hell purists who thrive on the most intricate and insane bullet patterns and score multipliers, at least if that's all they want.

We're trying to cater to everyone who's into action games and shooters, Xenoraid just happens to be broadly in a genre that is largely very particular these days (bullet hell). So we made Xenoraid much more casual, which is not to say easy; there's a Hard Mode after completing the game once, and the Survival will be very tricky in 15 minutes.

[url=http://www.cubed3.com/review/3135/1/xenoraid-pc.html]Cubed3[/url]
 scored the game 7 out of 10: 

[quote=Cubed3]... features several welcome departures from the current state of the genre that have been implemented to a high level of technical excellence and design, delivering a very enjoyable game that becomes more enjoyable the more it is played. It is definitely one that can get its hooks into you.[/quote]

We could listen to compliments like "high level of technical excellence and design" all day, every day. Thanks!

A big thank you also to each and every one who bought the game! We hope you enjoy playing the game. If you happen to have friends who might be into this kind of stuff, itIt'd be a big favour for us if you could spread the word about the game.

We just really enjoy shooting in itself, and we wanted to make a game that was very much about [i]shooting[/i]. [quote=the10kan]I very much like the way enemy ships react to player actions rather than just moving in scripted formations. Most alien ships have guns with a fixed arc of fire, and they actively maneuver to line up shots on you or to avoid colliding with asteroids. [/quote]

Yes, exactly this! We found out quickly that the awesome shooting mechanics we had in the game work the best in conjuction with as dynamic combat as we can get. Which is great, because that was our assumption and plan all along! We also wanted to inject as much "space dogfighting" feeling into the game as the broad vertically scrolling shoot'em up genre limits permit, and were happy with the way how it came out.

Xenoraid - no to memorizing challenges, yes to piloting and shooting challenges.

[quote=Likconater(of the Gamerholics Anonymous fame)]Fantastic! Looking for a bullet hell game? Xenoraid has got you covered, truth is we didnt go into this game expecting alot but once we started playing it we just couldnt stop[/quote]

We're always happy to please :) We always felt like marketing and positioning Xenoraid is not easy, but at least we seem to be winning over people once they give the game a go.

[quote=stubar]I'd recommend Xenoraid to anyone looking for a thinking man/womans shoot 'em up![/quote]

Amen, brother. Amen.

Well, to be fair, at about 10 minute point in Survival I'm not sure I'm able to think much, it seems to be all about the lizard brain right about at that time :)

[h1]Critic reviews[/h1]

The game hasn't been widely picked up by gaming sites for critic reviews, but we're expecting more to come. The haul thus far has been great!

[url=http://www.brashgames.co.uk/2016/10/06/xenoraid-review/]Brash Games[/url]
 gave the game a perfect 10 out of 10 review score:

[quote=Brash Games]From the second I started playing this game it had my full attention, it was an incredible experience and I got lost in hours of gameplay.[/quote]

This almost made us cry a little.

[url=http://www.gamingcypher.com/xenoraid-review-pc/]Gaming Cypher[/url]
 awarded the game 8.5 out of 10: 

[quote=Gaming Cypher]If you are a casual gamer who needs to kill some time, or even a competitive gamer for the leaderboards, you may want to add this game to your stockpile.[/quote]

Yes, we feel the game should definitely go into a whole lot of stockpiles. Hundreds, thousands of stockpiles!

[url=http://operationrainfall.com/2016/10/04/review-xenoraid/]Operation Rainfall[/url]
 gave the game a solid 4 out of 5 stars: 

[quote=Operation Rainfall]Shmup experts may find the game less difficult than some bullet hell games for example, but the game still requires accuracy and good timing.[/quote]

Yes! We always knew the game wouldn't appeal to bullet hell purists who thrive on the most intricate and insane bullet patterns and score multipliers, at least if that's all they want.

We're trying to cater to everyone who's into action games and shooters, Xenoraid just happens to be broadly in a genre that is largely very particular these days (bullet hell). So we made Xenoraid much more casual, which is not to say easy; there's a Hard Mode after completing the game once, and the Survival will be very tricky in 15 minutes.

[url=http://www.cubed3.com/review/3135/1/xenoraid-pc.html]Cubed3[/url]
 scored the game 7 out of 10: 

[quote=Cubed3]... features several welcome departures from the current state of the genre that have been implemented to a high level of technical excellence and design, delivering a very enjoyable game that becomes more enjoyable the more it is played. It is definitely one that can get its hooks into you.[/quote]

We could listen to compliments like "high level of technical excellence and design" all day, every day. Thanks!

A big thank you also to each and every one who bought the game! We hope you enjoy playing the game. If you happen to have friends who might be into this kind of stuff, itIt'd be a big favour for us if you could spread the word about the game.

Xenoraid is launching today in Steam!

A big thank you to all the beta testers, previewers, YouTubers and streamers for your pre-release feedback and coverage. The game is better because of your input and far more people have heard of it than we could have ever reached by ourselves.

If you're discovering the game just now, welcome! Go ahead and check it out. If you purchase and enjoy the game, great! Please let us know your thoughts in the Steam discussion forums. We plan to update the game in a couple of weeks, so all feedback is much welcomed.

Happy hunting, starfighters!

notes.title: Xenoraid launching on September 30th!
notes.notes:
We have a launch date: September 30th! That's... Really soon!

We have also announced the pricepoint, which is $9.99 USD. There will be a launch week discount as well, -10% or thereabouts.

We ask everyone to join us in spreading the word about the game, and it'd be the greatest thing if we got as many gamers as possible to add the game to their wishlist. That would help us make the most out of the release notification emails Steam sends when the game becomes available. That, in turn, will help us get those oh so important launch day sales and earn considerably more visibility on the Steam frontpage.

We will use the remaining time we have to fine tune and polish the game, and to run tests to eliminate as many technical issues as we can. At this time it's looking pretty good, the game runs great and robust!

If you have any thoughts about the game or just want to say hi, head on over to the discussion forums!
